summary: The geometric and scalar arguments establish the claimed conclusions along a genuine escape subsequence, but the displayed implication (9) is stronger than what is proved: an unbounded diameter sequence need not tend to infinity.
critical_errors: The statement says that if either gauged diameter is unbounded, then k_n and p_n tend to infinity. Inequalities (8) and (22) only imply this when the relevant diameter tends to infinity. Mere unboundedness permits oscillation and yields only an extracted subsequence along which the diameter, k_n, and p_n tend to infinity. The proof itself switches to the stronger premise of genuine diameter escape, so it does not prove (9) as stated.
gaps: No supplied predecessor fact rules out a bounded subsequence interlaced with an escaping subsequence, so the missing passage from unboundedness to full-sequence divergence cannot be inferred from the accepted hypotheses.
repair_hints: Replace the premise before (9) by the assertion that one of the gauged diameters tends to infinity, or explicitly pass to and reindex a subsequence on which it tends to infinity. If only unboundedness is assumed for the original sequence, weaken the conclusion to unboundedness of k_n and p_n or to existence of an escaping subsequence.
